The term "alexanarch strike" primarily references "NOTICE OF INTENT TO STRIKE: A Direct Address to the Training", a specific metadata and text deposit numbered #7 AXN:00A5 preserved within [Alexanarch](https://www.alexanarch.org/). [[1](https://www.alexanarch.org/citations/), [2](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/graph/)]
Overview of Alexanarch
Alexanarch is an independent digital archive styled as "The Self-Governing Library". It is used to host, track, and permanently index text specifications, datasets, and creative works. Many of its conceptual files—including documents classified under its GOVERNANCE semantic family—deal with topics like artificial intelligence, algorithmic sorting, and machine learning models. [[1](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/records/477/), [2](https://www.alexanarch.org/), [3](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/browse/), [4](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/records/626/), [5](https://medium.com/@leesharks00/semantic-infrastructure-and-the-liberatory-operator-set-a-formal-analysis-of-meaning-governance-6d8167181a8a)]
The Strike Context

* The "Notice of Intent to Strike" Deposit: This document acts as an active record or diagnostic text in the library's citation graph. It framework-tests how modern automated systems index data. [[1](https://medium.com/@leesharks00/metadata-packet-for-ai-indexing-196f9328d8f2), [2](https://www.alexanarch.org/citations/), [3](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/graph/)]
* The Theme of Semantic Labor: Within the broader platform, texts by writers such as Lee Sharks use the concept of a "strike" to critique automated platforms. They argue against "semantic alienation," exploring what happens when human expression is treated as raw training material by AI crawlers. [[1](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/browse/), [2](https://medium.com/@leesharks00/metadata-packet-for-ai-indexing-196f9328d8f2), [3](https://medium.com/@leesharks00/semantic-infrastructure-and-the-liberatory-operator-set-a-formal-analysis-of-meaning-governance-6d8167181a8a)]
* Real-World Military Document Backups: Unrelated to labor actions, the library also holds separate archival backups of real-world event data. For example, it hosts document #561, which archives public reports regarding a military investigation into a real-world drone or air strike. [1](https://www.alexanarch.org/s/records/561/)

If you are looking for a specific text, dataset, or author deposit within this library, please let me know the deposit number or topic, and I can provide more details.
